what_it_does: Predicting how fast a CPU will run a program is crucial for chip design but traditionally requires either slow detailed simulations or fast but inaccurate pure machine-learning models. Concorde combines both: it uses first-principles mathematical equations to model the CPU's fundamental behavior (pipeline stages, caches, branch prediction, memory delays) to capture the core physics, then trains a machine-learning model only to fix the small gaps between the equation-based prediction and reality. This hybrid approach runs fast enough for exploring thousands of chip designs while maintaining accuracy across different CPU architectures and programs.
